title: Mind Your Margin and Boundary: Are Your Distilled Datasets Truly Robust?
claim: Existing methods ignore the smallest robust margins and weak class separation; ours targets both with a curriculum and a contrastive loss.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line; left concept, right pipeline, yellow dashed links
description: The figure has two halves split by a vertical dashed line. The left half is a large circle with robustness (red, vertical) and accuracy (blue, horizontal) axes. It holds a synthetic-dataset stack, a pink concentric 'Robust Risk' blob marked with 'Smallest Robust Margins', and a dashed 'Decision Boundary' region. Teal squares, green triangles and orange circles sit around the boundary, with a blue arrow labeled 'Inter-class Separation'. Two yellow dashed arrows run from these two issues to the right half. The right half is a pipeline: an Original Dataset stack goes into an LS-PGD and Perturbation Score block, which produces s(x) bars and an Adversarial Dataset. The Contrastive Learning block then feeds a class-balanced memory queue with a loss symbol, and the output is a Synthetic Dataset. The eye goes first to the colored axes and the red risk blob.
caption: Existing robust DD struggles to balance robustness and accuracy by (i) ignoring that robust risk is driven by the smallest margins and (ii) failing to separate classes near decision boundaries. C$^2$R addresses this with an attack-aware curriculum that prioritizes small-margin adversaries and a contrastive robustness loss.
abstract: Dataset distillation (DD) compresses a large training set into a small synthetic set for efficient training, but most DD methods optimize only clean accuracy and leave robustness uncontrolled. Recent robust DD methods improve robustness, yet they often suffer from a poor accuracy-robustness trade-off because they (i) treat all adversarially perturbed examples uniformly, despite robust risk being dominated by near-zero robust margins, and (ii) do not explicitly increase inter-class separation in the decision boundary where attacks concentrate. We present Contrastive Curriculum for Robust Dataset Distillation (C$^2$R), a framework that couples an attack-aware curriculum with a contrastive robustness objective. From a robust-margin perspective, we derive a perturbation score that approximates each sample's robust hinge, enabling a curriculum that prioritizes the smallest-margin adversaries that most directly drive robust error. In parallel, a class-balanced contrastive robustness loss enforces adversarial invariance while explicitly widening boundary separation across classes. Experiments on CIFAR-10/100, Tiny-ImageNet, and multiple ImageNet-1K subsets under six attacks show that C$^2$R achieves the best robust accuracy, outperforming prior robust DD by $2.8$% on average.
